summary:
Our project is a **Smart Vision and Navigation System** designed to improve safe movement in challenging environments. We developed a compact smart-glasses prototype using an **ESP32, ultrasonic sensors, and a mobile application** to detect nearby obstacles and provide real-time guidance to the user.

The system was designed with two important applications in mind: **supporting astronauts during lunar surface exploration** and **assisting people with visual impairments on Earth**. For astronauts, the system can help identify obstacles and unsafe paths around lunar landing and exploration areas, while also enabling path information to be recorded for safer navigation. For visually impaired users, the glasses can provide obstacle alerts and directional assistance without requiring constant visual attention.

The project addresses the challenge of **safe, independent navigation in unfamiliar or hazardous environments** by combining low-cost sensors, embedded computing, and mobile connectivity. This is important because better situational awareness can reduce collision risks, improve mobility, and support safer exploration and accessibility.
details:
What does the project do and how does it work?

Our project, Smart Vision & Navigation System, is a compact wearable technology designed to help users navigate safely by detecting obstacles and providing real-time guidance. The smart glasses use ultrasonic sensors connected to an ESP32 to detect objects in the user’s surroundings. Sensor data is processed by the ESP32 and communicated with a mobile application through wireless connectivity. The system can provide obstacle alerts and directional information, helping the user choose a safer path. We also designed the concept to record navigation/path information so previously travelled routes can support safer movement.

What are the benefits?

The system provides hands-free, real-time environmental awareness. For astronauts, it can help identify obstacles and support safer movement around lunar landing and exploration areas. For people with visual impairments, it can provide an additional layer of obstacle awareness and navigation assistance.

Intended impact

Our goal is to make navigation safer, more accessible, and more independent. The lunar application demonstrates how affordable sensing technology could support future exploration, while the accessibility application addresses a practical challenge faced by visually impaired users on Earth.

Tools, hardware, and software

  • ESP32 microcontroller
  • Ultrasonic sensors for obstacle detection
  • Smart-glasses wearable prototype
  • Android mobile application
  • Android Studio
  • Kotlin/Java for mobile development
  • Arduino/C++ for ESP32 programming
  • Wireless communication between the ESP32 and mobile device

What makes the project creative?

The project combines wearable technology, embedded systems, mobile connectivity, obstacle detection, and navigation into a compact platform. Instead of creating a solution only for one environment, we explored a dual-purpose concept: the same core technology can support both future lunar exploration and accessibility on Earth.

What factors did the team consider?

We considered compact size, low cost, power consumption, sensor accuracy, response time, wireless connectivity, ease of use, reliability, and user safety. We also considered the limitations of ultrasonic sensing and designed the system as an assistive technology rather than a replacement for existing navigation or safety systems.
